params.place: on the map: an old English city, split down the middle

moments.what: the east half of the city plan turns grey, its streets crowded
a dividing line draws down the middle of the city
the label OLD ENGLISH CITY writes on
a red-cross pennant pops up on the town hall
the river through the city shimmers
a big question mark drops onto the grey east side

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Why is the east side of so many old English cities the poorer side?

params.place: on the map: England, its old cities pinned

moments.what: a pin drops on London and splits into a green west and a grey east
pins drop on the mill towns, Manchester, Leeds, Sheffield
the camera slides north up England
every pin splits green west, grey east
a magnifying glass sweeps over the map
the glass presses on the land and finds nothing
the glass lifts and swirls of wind appear over the map

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: From London to the mill towns of the north, it happens again and again. And the reason isn't on the ground. It's in the air.

params.place: on the map: Britain and the Atlantic to its west

moments.what: the camera pulls out to show the Atlantic west of Britain
a weathervane rises on the map and spins
long wind arrows sweep in from the ocean
the weathervane points west, the label WEST WIND writes on
ATLANTIC OCEAN writes across the sea
the arrows run right across Britain
NORTH SEA writes on beyond the east coast

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Most days, Britain's wind blows in from the west, off the Atlantic Ocean, right across the country to the North Sea.

params.place: on the map: England, a chimney rising at every city

moments.what: factory chimneys rise at the city pins
coal heaps pile beside the chimneys, smoke puffs
a surveyor stands on the map with a clipboard
a counter board plants on the map and counts up the chimneys
more chimneys pop up across England
the camera eases back over the whole country
a COAL AGE stamp lands on the board

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then came the factories, burning coal. Researchers have mapped about 5,000 of their chimneys in England's cities in the eighteen eighties.

params.place: on the map: the city plan, smoke drifting east

moments.what: wind arrows blow across the city from the west
the arrows gust harder and the pennant streams east
smoke pours from the chimneys and leans east
a black cloud rolls across the city
the cloud settles over the east half
the east streets go dark grey under it
DOWNWIND writes on under the cloud
the cloud swells, day after day
a question mark puffs out of the cloud

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And the west wind did what wind does. It carried all that smoke east, over the streets downwind, day after day. So who had to breathe it?

params.place: on the map: the west side of the city, upwind

moments.what: a family in top hats stands on the map
they lift a bag of coins
a horse carriage rolls west against the arrows
big villas pop up on the west side
green gardens and trees fill in around them
the sky over the west turns bright
the west half traces in green

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Families who could pay moved upwind, into big houses with gardens on the clean west side.

params.place: on the map: the east side of the city, downwind

moments.what: a line of mill workers stands on the east side
their pockets turn out empty
the camera slides east into the smoke
rows of tiny houses pack in
the terraced rows join end to end
soot flakes fall and the east traces in grey
the workers cough as the cloud rolls over them

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Workers who couldn't stayed east, in cheap terraced streets under the soot, breathing everyone else's smoke.

params.place: on the map: the same city, the mills shut

moments.what: the chimneys topple one by one
a CLOSED board nails onto a mill
the black cloud breaks up
the sky over the city turns blue
the camera pushes to the dividing line
the dividing line glows red
the line stamps down hard, west still green, east still grey

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then the mills closed, and the air cleared. And the strange part? The split stayed.

params.place: on the map: the modern city, two halves

moments.what: a moving van drives into the green west
a family steps out at a villa
a second van drives into the grey east
a family carries boxes into a terrace
modern cars and buses run along the streets
the camera pulls back over both halves
the vans drive in again, again and again

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Rich streets kept pulling in rich families, and cheap streets kept pulling in the poor, long after the smoke was gone, generation after generation.

params.place: on the map: England in the census year, the city pins split

moments.what: the census board with the year drops onto the map
the city pins pulse
the COAL AGE tag peels off the census board
the census board swings on its post
a ghost of the old smoke drifts across the map
the camera pushes in on the ghost smoke over the cities
a share board plants on the map, its bar filling
the UP TO board lands beside the census board
the share bar fills to its mark
the camera pulls back over England, every pin split
the west halves glow green
the east halves glow grey

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In 2011, more than a century later, that old smoke still explains up to 20% of how England's neighbourhoods split into rich and poor.

params.place: on the map: back to the old English city, split down the middle

moments.what: the west half of the city pulses green
the east half pulses grey
a comment bubble pops up over the river
the camera glides to the first frame
the comment bubble wobbles
the bubble pops away
the weathervane on the town hall spins
the vane points west, an arrow sweeps east
the question mark starts to drop onto the east side

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: West side or east side: which half of your city is the rich one? Tell me below. And next time you're there, check the wind, and ask:
